The views and opinions of authors expressed herein do not necessarily state or reflectthoseoftheUnitedStatesGovernmentoranyagencythereof. 1 ABSTRACT This project advances a unified, open-source framework for the optimal co-design of thermal, electrical, and control systems in grid-interactive efficient districts (GEDs). As communitiesintegrategrowinglevelsofdistributedenergyresources,traditionalapproaches thatmodelthermalandelectricalnetworksindependentlyleadtoreducedefficiency,limited flexibility, and missed opportunities for coordinated operation. To address these challenges, the research team developed a comprehensive suite of physics-based models, control algo- rithms, and software tools that enable holistic simulation, optimization, and demonstration ofdistrict-scaleenergysystems. The project delivers several major contributions: (1) new open-source microgrid and inverter models based on the Western Electricity Coordinating Council’s specifications, val- idatedthroughbothindustry-standardsimulationtoolsandpower-hardware-in-the-Loopex- periments; (2) coupled thermal–electrical component and system models, including induc- tion machines, HVAC equipment, and combined heat-and-power systems; (3) advanced op- timization and reinforcement-learning–based control strategies for microgrids and district energy plants; and (4) seamless integration of these models and algorithms into the Na- tionalLaboratoryoftheRockies’URBANoptplatformfordistrict-scaledesignandanalysis. ThefullworkflowsupportsautomatedtranslationfromGIS-baseddistrictrepresentationsto high-fidelity Modelica system models, enabling robust evaluation of alternative configura- tionsandoperationalstrategies.
